header: ZU-MED-105 · Professional Practice I, 32 single-best-answer questions authored from mcq شامل.pdf (the tier-2 bank catalogued but not opened by pp1-cluster1/2), all from its Self-Directed-Learning section (pages 2-11 of 44). Keys recovered via a yellow fill-rectangle highlight over the correct option, detected with an ad hoc read-only PyMuPDF script matching each fill's bounding box to the option line it overlaps (not in the shared toolchain, source-specific, matching the ad hoc-script precedent set by cluster1/2's own gray-fill detection for a different source). Render-confirmed on pages 2 and 26 this pass (2 renders, both matched the script's output exactly, including a genuinely unmarked pair of questions on page 26). 133 of 142 detected question blocks in the full 44-page bank are keyed this way (~94%), comfortably over the 60% approval bar; this cluster authors only the Self-Directed-Learning section, which is entirely new territory in this module (lanes 1-2's 62 questions never touch SDL). One item (pp1shamel-q05) printed 6 options; trimmed to 5 by dropping the weakest distractor ('Time and effort saving', still a genuine function per the source, listed in the backing concept's own definition) and keeping the exception-marked correct answer, per the module's >5-options-trimmed-and-documented rule. The bank's bioethics-principles, consent/confidentiality, vulnerability/dignity, leadership/team-dynamics and health-determinants sections (pages 12-40) are triaged (keyed, method validated) but not authored this pass, several of their facts sit too close to lane1/2's existing concepts (Grow's SDL stage model, vertical equity, genetic-factors-non-modifiable-determinant) or to internal duplicates within this same source to mint cleanly without further per-item review; real remaining scope for a follow-up pass. See coverage/ZU-MED-105-triage.md and coverage/ZU-MED-105-triage-keys.txt for the full method and the per-question map.

questions.title: Definition of learning
questions.question: Is the process of acquiring new understanding, knowledge, behaviors, skills, values, attitudes, and preferences. Refer to…

explanations.A: Incorrect. Self-directed learning is one particular way of carrying out this general acquisition process, driven by the learner's own initiative, but the stem describes the broader process itself, not that one specific way of pursuing it.
explanations.B: Correct. This is the standard, general definition of learning: the process of acquiring new understanding, knowledge, behaviours, skills, values, attitudes and preferences. It is the umbrella term for the acquisition process itself, before any particular method, such as self-directed learning or teaching, is specified. The stem matches this general definition word for word.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Learning materials are the resources and devices used to support learning, not the process of acquiring new understanding itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Teaching describes an instructor's activity of imparting knowledge to others, which is a different process from the learner's own acquisition of understanding described in the stem.

questions.learning_objective: State the general definition of learning as the process of acquiring new understanding, knowledge, behaviours, skills, values, attitudes and preferences.

questions.title: Definition of self-directed learning
questions.question: A process in which individuals take the initiative, with or without the help of other. refer to

explanations.A: Correct. This is the definition of self-directed learning (SDL): a process in which individuals take the initiative, with or without the help of others, to identify and pursue their own learning. Learner-driven initiative is the specific feature that distinguishes SDL from learning in general. The stem names this initiative-taking element directly, which is why SDL is the answer rather than the broader term 'learning'.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Learning in general does not require the learner to take the initiative; it can be driven entirely by a teacher or curriculum, unlike the initiative-taking process the stem describes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Learning materials are physical or digital resources used to support learning, not a description of who initiates the learning process.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Teaching is directed by an instructor rather than by the learner's own initiative, the opposite of what the stem describes.

questions.learning_objective: State that self-directed learning is defined by the learner taking the initiative, with or without help from others, rather than by working alone.

questions.title: Definition of learning materials
questions.question: Learning materials ……..

options.A: The resources that teachers use to assist learners to meet the expectations for learning are defined by curriculum.
options.B: implementing appropriate learning strategies, and evaluating learning outcomes.
options.C: Are those procedures and devices that help to make teaching and learning more integrating, stimulating, reinforcing, and effective.

explanations.A: Incorrect. This describes only the curriculum-alignment role of learning materials; this source marks the combination of this description together with option C as the complete answer.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Implementing strategies and evaluating outcomes describes an instructor's broader teaching activity, not the specific definition of learning materials themselves.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This describes only the procedures-and-devices role of learning materials; on its own it omits the curriculum-alignment role named in option A, which this source also marks as part of the correct answer.
explanations.D: Correct. This source defines learning materials as combining both roles together: the curriculum-aligned resources teachers use to help learners meet learning expectations (A), and the procedures and devices that make teaching and learning more integrating, stimulating, reinforcing and effective (C). Neither description alone is treated as complete; the combination is what this source marks as correct.

questions.learning_objective: State that learning materials combine curriculum-aligned teacher resources with the procedures and devices that make teaching and learning more effective.

questions.title: Types of learning resources
questions.question: Types of learning resources

explanations.A: Incorrect. Audio resources are a genuine type of learning resource, but this source recognises visual and visual-audio resources as further types, not covered by naming audio alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Visual resources are a genuine type, but naming this one type alone leaves out audio and combined visual-audio resources.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Visual-audio resources, which combine both sensory channels, are a genuine type, but this option alone omits the separate audio-only and visual-only categories.
explanations.D: Correct. This source classifies learning resources into three types: audio, visual, and combined visual-audio resources. All three are recognised types rather than any one being the sole correct category, which is why the complete answer names all of them together.

questions.learning_objective: List audio, visual and visual-audio as the types of learning resources this source recognises.

questions.title: Functions of learning resources, except
questions.question: Functions of learning resources all except

explanations.A: Incorrect. Promoting critical thinking is one of this source's genuine functions of learning resources, so it is not the exception the question asks for.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Encouraging participation is a genuine function this source lists, not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Capturing attention and interest is a genuine function this source lists, not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Engaging the maximum number of senses is a genuine function this source lists, not the exception.
explanations.E: Correct. This source lists five genuine functions of learning resources, promoting critical thinking, encouraging participation, capturing attention and interest, saving time and effort, and engaging the maximum senses, but does not name 'increasing hope' among them. Because an emotional outcome like hope is not one of the functions this source credits to learning resources, it is the exception the 'all except' question is testing for.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that increasing hope is not among this source's listed functions of learning resources, unlike promoting critical thinking, participation, attention, efficiency and use of the senses.

questions.title: Benefits of self-directed learning
questions.question: Importance / Benefits of Self-directed learning

explanations.A: Incorrect. Building soft skills is one genuine benefit this source names, but it is combined with two further benefits this source also credits, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Encouraging independence in learning is a genuine benefit, but naming it alone omits the other two benefits this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Creating a collaborative learning environment is a genuine benefit, but naming it alone omits the individual-skill benefits this source also credits.
explanations.D: Correct. This source names three benefits of self-directed learning together: building important soft skills, encouraging independence in learning, and creating a collaborative learning environment. Because SDL is learner-initiated, it might seem purely individual, but this source explicitly credits it with a collaborative benefit as well, alongside the individual ones, which is why all three combine into the correct answer.

questions.learning_objective: List building soft skills, encouraging independence, and creating a collaborative learning environment as the benefits of self-directed learning this source names together.

questions.title: Methods of self-directed learning
questions.question: Methods of Self-directed learning: The two broad subdivisions of Self-directed learning are:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Facilitated learning is one of the two genuine subdivisions this source names, but naming it alone omits the second subdivision, self-paced learning.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Self-paced learning is one of the two genuine subdivisions this source names, but naming it alone omits facilitated learning.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Providing a template is offered only as a distractor in this question, not as one of the two genuine method subdivisions this source names.
explanations.D: Correct. This source divides self-directed-learning methods into two broad subdivisions: facilitated learning (A) and self-paced learning (B), and marks their combination as the correct answer. Facilitated learning still involves guidance from someone else, while self-paced learning is driven entirely by the learner, so together the two subdivisions cover the full range of how SDL can be structured.
explanations.E: Incorrect. This pairs self-paced learning with 'providing a template', but this source marks providing a template only as a distractor, not as one of the two genuine method subdivisions.

questions.learning_objective: State that facilitated learning and self-paced learning are the two broad subdivisions of self-directed-learning methods this source names.

questions.title: Definition of self-paced learning
questions.question: needs the learner to be motivated, oriented towards learning, and competent to choose suitable resources for the required content . refer to…..

explanations.A: Incorrect. Facilitated learning still involves guidance and structure supplied by someone else, unlike the learner-alone motivation and resource-selection the stem describes.
explanations.B: Correct. Self-paced learning needs the learner to be motivated, oriented towards learning, and competent to choose suitable resources for the required content, entirely on their own, without another person setting the pace. This matches the stem's description exactly, distinguishing it from facilitated learning, which still relies on outside guidance.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Providing a template describes a support tool, not the personal qualities of motivation, orientation and resource-selection competence the stem is describing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This combines facilitated learning with self-paced learning, but facilitated learning does not match the learner-alone description in the stem.
explanations.E: Incorrect. This combines self-paced learning with providing a template, but providing a template is a support tool, not the personal-competence description the stem gives.

questions.learning_objective: State that self-paced learning requires the learner to be motivated, oriented towards learning, and competent to choose suitable resources independently.

questions.title: Steps to implement SDL, except
questions.question: Steps to implement self-directed learning: all true except

options.D: Adjust and adapt to suit doctor needs

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assessing student readiness is a genuine step in implementing self-directed learning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Setting goals for learning is a genuine step in implementing self-directed learning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Engaging students in the process is a genuine step in implementing self-directed learning, so it is not the exception.
explanations.D: Correct. The genuine final step in implementing self-directed learning is to adjust and adapt the approach to suit student needs, not doctor needs. Because SDL implementation should be adapted around the learner rather than around an unrelated party such as a physician role, 'suit doctor needs' is the false, out-of-place option, making it the exception this 'all true except' question is testing for.

questions.learning_objective: State that the adapt step in implementing self-directed learning means adjusting the approach to suit student needs, and recognise 'doctor needs' as a false substitution for that step.

questions.title: Goal-setting step in implementing SDL
questions.question: Goals provide students with the freedom necessary to study in their own way while adhering to firm rules to complete their work. Refer to which Steps to implement self-directed learning is….

options.D: Adjust and adapt to suit doctor needs

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assessing student readiness is a separate, earlier step concerned with whether the student is prepared to begin, not with the freedom-and-firm-rules balance the stem describes.
explanations.B: Correct. Setting goals for learning is the step that gives students the freedom necessary to study in their own way, while still adhering to the firm rules needed to complete their work. This balance between learner freedom and structural rules matches the stem exactly, distinguishing it from the other implementation steps in this source's four-step sequence.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Engaging students in the process concerns active participation, not the specific freedom-versus-firm-rules balance the stem describes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This source marks 'adjust and adapt to suit doctor needs' as the false, out-of-place step elsewhere in its material, and it does not match the freedom-and-firm-rules description in this stem either.

questions.learning_objective: State that setting goals for learning is the SDL implementation step that gives students freedom to study their own way while still requiring firm rules to complete the work.

questions.title: Adapt-to-student-needs step in implementing SDL
questions.question: Teachers often blend this learning method within classroom education to suit the needs and growth of students . Refer to which Steps to implement self-directed learning is….

options.D: Adjust and adapt to suit student needs

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assessing student readiness concerns judging preparedness before beginning, not blending the method within classroom education to suit ongoing student needs and growth.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Setting goals for learning concerns the freedom-and-firm-rules balance described elsewhere in this source, not the blending-within-classroom-education description in this stem.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Engaging students in the process concerns active participation, not specifically the adaptation to suit changing student needs and growth the stem describes.
explanations.D: Correct. The step of adjusting and adapting to suit student needs is what allows teachers to blend self-directed learning within classroom education, suiting the approach to each student's needs and growth. This is the same 'adapt' step this source elsewhere marks as false when misdirected toward 'doctor needs' instead, here it is correctly matched to student needs, exactly as the stem describes.

questions.learning_objective: State that the adapt step in implementing self-directed learning means adjusting the approach to suit student needs, and recognise 'doctor needs' as a false substitution for that step.

questions.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of learning
questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of learning include….

options.A: Frequent evaluation allows students to reflect on their learning and progress.
options.D: Regularly thinking about what they have learned is helpful.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Frequent evaluation and reflection is one genuine practice this source names, but it is combined with three further practices this source also credits, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Consulting with the teacher is a genuine practice, but naming it alone omits the other practices this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Seeking feedback is a genuine practice, but naming it alone omits the other practices this source lists.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Regularly reflecting on what has been learned is a genuine practice, but naming it alone omits the other practices this source lists.
explanations.E: Correct. This source lists four practices for evaluating the effectiveness of learning together: frequent evaluation and reflection, consulting the teacher, seeking feedback, and regularly thinking about what has been learned. Combining self-reflection with external consultation and deliberate feedback-seeking gives a more complete picture of whether learning has actually been effective than any single practice alone, which is why all four combine into the correct answer.

questions.learning_objective: List frequent evaluation, teacher consultation, feedback-seeking, and regular reflection together as this source's practices for evaluating the effectiveness of learning.

questions.title: Competencies of self-directed learners, except
questions.question: All are the Competencies of Self-directed learners . except.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Self-awareness is a genuine competency this source lists for self-directed learners, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Critical appraisal is a genuine competency this source lists, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Critical thinking is a genuine competency this source lists, so it is not the exception.
explanations.D: Correct. This source names four genuine competencies of self-directed learners: self-awareness, critical appraisal, critical thinking, and reflection. 'Evaluating the professionalism' is not among them; the four genuine competencies describe internal cognitive and reflective capacities a learner directs at their own learning, a different category from judging professionalism as an external standard, which is why it is the exception here.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Reflection is a genuine competency this source lists, so it is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that evaluating professionalism is not among this source's listed competencies of self-directed learners, unlike self-awareness, critical appraisal, critical thinking and reflection.

questions.title: Process of self-directed learning
questions.question: Process of self-directed learning include

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assessing the task at hand is one genuine part of the SDL process this source names, but it is combined with two further parts, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Evaluating one's own strengths and weaknesses is a genuine part of the process, but naming it alone omits the other parts this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Practising and monitoring one's own performance is a genuine part of the process, but naming it alone omits the other parts this source lists.
explanations.D: Correct. This source describes the process of self-directed learning as including assessing the task at hand, evaluating one's own strengths and weaknesses, and practising and monitoring one's own performance, together. This process is inherently self-referential: the learner assesses the task, judges their own capability against it, and then monitors their own execution, rather than an external party performing any of these steps, which is why all three combine into the correct answer.

questions.learning_objective: List assessing the task, evaluating one's own strengths and weaknesses, and practising and monitoring one's own performance together as the process of self-directed learning this source describes.

questions.title: Belief factor in the SDL process
questions.question: In the Process of self-directed learning

options.A: Student s belief about intelligence and learning

explanations.A: Correct. Within the process of self-directed learning, this source marks the student's belief about intelligence and learning itself as the relevant mindset factor. How a student thinks about whether intelligence and ability can grow through effort shapes how willingly that student takes the initiative the definition of SDL requires, which is why this specific belief, rather than belief about reality, love or hope, is the one this source ties to the SDL process.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Belief about reality in general is not the mindset factor this source ties to the SDL process; only belief about intelligence and learning is named.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Belief about love is not the mindset factor this source ties to the SDL process; only belief about intelligence and learning is named.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Belief about hope is not the mindset factor this source ties to the SDL process; only belief about intelligence and learning is named.

questions.learning_objective: State that a student's belief about intelligence and learning, rather than belief about reality, love or hope, is the factor this source names within the SDL process.

questions.title: Definition of a learning plan
questions.question: A learning plan is…………..

options.A: a document designed to help you reflect upon and structure your learning for success in examinations and your career in general practice.
options.B: based upon self-reflection and an objective evaluation of your skills and knowledge.
options.C: a set of skills that can be taught, learned, and acquired

explanations.A: Incorrect. This describes the document-and-structure role of a learning plan, but this source marks the combination of this description together with option B as the correct, complete answer.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This describes the self-reflection-and-evaluation basis of a learning plan, but on its own it omits the document-and-structure description in option A, which this source also marks as part of the correct answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Describing a learning plan as merely a set of skills that can be taught, learned and acquired is a distractor this source does not mark as correct.
explanations.D: Correct. This source defines a learning plan by combining two descriptions together: it is a document designed to help a learner reflect upon and structure their learning for success in examinations and their career (A), and it is based upon self-reflection combined with an objective evaluation of the learner's own skills and knowledge (B). A learning plan is therefore both a concrete document and a process grounded in honest self-evaluation, not simply a skill someone possesses.
explanations.E: Incorrect. This source marks only the combination of A and B as correct, not all four options including the 'set of skills' distractor in C.

questions.learning_objective: State that a learning plan is a document for structuring learning toward exam and career success, grounded in self-reflection and objective self-evaluation.

questions.title: Aims of a learning plan
questions.question: A learning plan aims to:

options.A: place you at the center of the learning process, and use your current practice as the basis of learning
options.B: assist you to make informed choices about your education needs
options.C: assist you to integrate theory and practice into your work
options.D: enhance your motivation to learn and to ask appropriate questions of yourself and others

explanations.A: Incorrect. Centring on current practice is one genuine aim this source names, but it is combined with three further aims, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Supporting informed choices about education needs is a genuine aim, but naming it alone omits the other aims this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Integrating theory and practice is a genuine aim, but naming it alone omits the other aims this source lists.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Enhancing motivation and appropriate questioning is a genuine aim, but naming it alone omits the other aims this source lists.
explanations.E: Correct. This source lists four aims of a learning plan together: centring learning on current practice, supporting informed choices about education needs, integrating theory and practice, and enhancing motivation to learn and ask appropriate questions. Together these aims connect a learning plan's practical starting point, current practice, to its ultimate purpose of sustained motivation and better-integrated knowledge, which is why all four combine into the correct answer.

questions.learning_objective: List centring on current practice, supporting informed choices, integrating theory and practice, and enhancing motivation together as the aims of a learning plan this source names.

questions.title: Developing a learning plan
questions.question: To develop learning plan ….

options.A: needs must be identified and so learning goals can be formulated
options.B: Developing a learning plan consists of a cyclical process
options.C: You should depend on your self

explanations.A: Incorrect. Identifying needs so goals can be formulated is one genuine fact this source names, but it is combined with the cyclical-process fact in option B, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The cyclical-process fact is genuine, but on its own it omits the needs-then-goals fact in option A, which this source also marks as part of the correct answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Depending on yourself alone, without the structured needs-to-goals sequence this source describes, is a distractor this source does not mark as correct.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This source marks only the combination of A and B as correct, not all four options including the 'depend on yourself' distractor in C.
explanations.E: Correct. This source marks developing a learning plan as requiring both facts together: learning needs must first be identified so that learning goals can be formulated from them (A), and this development is part of a cyclical process rather than a one-off, linear task (B). Because the process is cyclical, a learning plan is expected to be revisited and updated as needs and goals change over time.

questions.learning_objective: State that developing a learning plan requires identifying learning needs to formulate goals, as part of a cyclical rather than one-off process.

questions.title: Uncovering gaps in knowledge
questions.question: According to methods to help you uncover the gaps in your knowledge the following are true

options.A: It is best to use more than one method
options.B: a combination of subjective and objective methods often gives a better overall picture of your knowledge gaps.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Using more than one method is genuine, but on its own it omits the specific subjective-and-objective-combination fact this source also marks correct in option B.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The subjective-and-objective-combination fact is genuine, but on its own it omits the general more-than-one-method fact in option A, which this source also marks as part of the correct answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Using only one method is the opposite of what this source recommends, and is not the correct answer.
explanations.D: Correct. This source marks the correct approach to uncovering gaps in knowledge as using more than one method (A), because a combination of subjective and objective methods together gives a better overall picture of a learner's knowledge gaps than either alone (B). Relying on a single method risks missing gaps that only a different type of method would reveal, which is why both facts combine into the correct answer.

questions.learning_objective: State that uncovering gaps in one's knowledge is best done by combining more than one method, including both subjective and objective approaches together.

questions.title: Learning-needs assessment methods
questions.question: Learning needs assessment methods:are

explanations.A: Incorrect. 360-degree appraisal is one genuine method this source names, but it is combined with two further methods, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Critical incident reviews are a genuine method, but naming this one alone omits the other methods this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Self-assessment is a genuine method, but naming this one alone omits the other methods this source lists.
explanations.D: Correct. This source names three learning-needs assessment methods together: 360-degree appraisal, critical incident reviews, and self-assessment. These draw on different sources of information, 360-degree appraisal gathers views from multiple people, critical incident reviews examine specific past events, and self-assessment relies on the learner's own judgement, so together they give several complementary ways to identify learning needs.

questions.title: Definition of practice reviews
questions.question: Could involve using data that already exist or doing a formal patient satisfaction questionnaire. Refer to……..

explanations.A: Incorrect. 360-degree appraisal gathers direct feedback from colleagues about the learner's own performance, not existing data or a patient satisfaction questionnaire.
explanations.B: Correct. Practice reviews, as a learning-needs assessment method, could involve using data that already exists or doing a formal patient satisfaction questionnaire, exactly as the stem describes. This distinguishes practice reviews from 360-degree appraisal, which instead gathers direct colleague feedback, and from self-assessment, which relies purely on the learner's own judgement.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Self-assessment relies on the learner's own judgement of their own performance, not on existing data or a formal patient satisfaction questionnaire.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Observation involves directly watching performance as it happens, not reviewing existing data or a formal satisfaction questionnaire.

questions.learning_objective: State that practice reviews use existing data or a formal patient satisfaction questionnaire, distinguishing this method from 360-degree appraisal and self-assessment.

questions.question: Steps to prioritize learning needs in a systematic and fair way

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assessing the situation is one genuine step this source names, but it is combined with three further steps, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Analyzing the data is a genuine step, but naming it alone omits the other steps this source lists.

explanations.E: Correct. questions.title: Assess-the-situation step
questions.question: Before you can prioritize learning needs, you need to assess the current situation. You can use various methods to collect data, such as observations, performance reviews, or tests refer to

explanations.A: Correct. Before learning needs can be prioritized, the current situation must first be assessed, using various methods to collect data such as observations, performance reviews, or tests, exactly as the stem describes. This is the first step in this source's four-step prioritisation sequence, and the quality of the data collected here shapes how well the later steps can work.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Analyzing the data is the step that follows data collection, not the initial assessment described in the stem.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Prioritizing the needs comes later in the sequence, after the situation has already been assessed and the data analyzed.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Communicating the results is the final step in the sequence, well after the initial situation-assessment the stem describes.

questions.learning_objective: State that assessing the situation using observations, performance reviews or tests is the first step in this source's sequence for prioritizing learning needs.

questions.title: Frameworks for prioritizing learning needs
questions.question: You can use different tools and frameworks to help you with this process, such as

explanations.A: Incorrect. The SWOT analysis is one genuine framework this source names, but it is combined with two further frameworks, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The KSA analysis is a genuine framework, but naming it alone omits the other frameworks this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The ADDIE model is a genuine framework, but naming it alone omits the other frameworks this source lists.

questions.title: Basis for prioritizing learning needs
questions.question: After you have identified the learning needs and their causes, you need to prioritize them based on :

explanations.A: Incorrect. Importance and urgency are one genuine criterion this source names, but combined with two further criteria, not the complete answer alone.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Feasibility, considering cost, time and resources, and impact are genuine criteria, but naming them alone omits the other criteria this source lists.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Relevance and demand are genuine criteria, but naming them alone omits the other criteria this source lists.
explanations.D: Correct. After learning needs and their causes have been identified, this source marks the basis for prioritizing them as importance and urgency, feasibility (cost, time and resources), and relevance and demand, taken together. Weighing all three criteria prevents prioritising a need that is important but currently infeasible, or one that is easy to address but not actually relevant or in demand.

questions.learning_objective: List importance and urgency, feasibility, and relevance and demand together as the basis this source names for prioritizing identified learning needs.

questions.title: Forms of evidence of learning

options.B: Identification of learning resources, supports and strategies
options.C: Identification of forms of evidence of learning
options.D: Specify timeframes and mode of contact

explanations.A: Incorrect. Identification of learning goals concerns what a learner intends to achieve, not the after-the-fact demonstration of learning the stem describes.

explanations.D: Incorrect. Specifying timeframes and mode of contact concerns scheduling and communication logistics, not the forms of evidence a learner will use to demonstrate learning.
